A_appropriateness_user_goal.decision: Keep the one-heavy-job cap and conservative resource admission. Repair the mismatch between sustained watchdog policy and permanent single-sample native refusal before spending another native run. No exact added capacity requirement is established.
A_appropriateness_user_goal.owner_requirement: Enforce a hard concurrency cap on simultaneous test runs, with a pre-flight resource check and a watchdog that refuses new launches above threshold rather than merely alerting. Resource exhaustion produces failures indistinguishable from product defects; prefer an overly conservative cap.
A_appropriateness_user_goal.authority: The owner requirement establishes safety and conservatism, not these fixed numeric CPU limits. PLAN.md section 3 explicitly calls numeric limits adjustable documented operational defaults and specifies two consecutive unsafe watches. Policy numeric settings trace to commit 76ba1292; reports/resource-review.json and resource-admission.json document agent review and implementation. No owner statement fixing these numeric values was found. Keep all numbers unchanged for the proposed repair.

B_implementation_quality.decision: The native boundary bypasses the guard temporal decision with its own permanent any-unsafe rule. This is a reproducible false-positive class relative to the stated sustained/two-consecutive policy, even though the latest physical CPU spike cannot be proven benign.
B_implementation_quality.sampling: cpuBusyFraction reads the second iostat row: a one-second busy interval. Preflight averages seven such intervals distributed across about 60 seconds, not continuous CPU measurement. Watch evaluates a single one-second interval about every 16 seconds (15-second wait plus sampling). Two snapshots are only an operational persistence proxy, not proof of continuous overload.
B_implementation_quality.current_transitions: reasons() compares each watch directly to >=.75 busy, or >=.60 busy plus load/logicalCPUs >=.75. The wrapper emits RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE immediately; only two consecutive bad samples create hold/stop and set resourceInvalid. Native requireNativeResourceHealth rejects any historical RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE regardless of current health or streak; awaitNativeResourceHealth waits only on stale_health. Thus CPU confirmation never occurs when the child exits at its next native boundary.
B_implementation_quality.origin: 12f43b3e introduced the native any-unsafe scan for EXT-D-0119. Its report says numeric policy unchanged, but the effective native temporal policy became stricter than PLAN.md and wrapper. Rejecting new actions while uncertain is correct; making a one-second CPU observation irrecoverably equivalent to sustained overload is the defect.
B_implementation_quality.verdict_gap: Latest wrapper final child_failed/resourceInvalid=false follows implementation: child exited before watchdog confirmation. It must not be read as resource-valid. A future unresolved CPU candidate or any confirmed unsafe run must finalize invalid-resource rather than child_failed or valid.

minimal_coherent_future_repair: Guard owns CPU temporal classification once. On first CPU-only threshold crossing, persist a distinct CPU_PENDING event containing the unchanged measured sample/reasons before allowing consumers to proceed. Do not emit legacy RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE for an unconfirmed CPU-only candidate. Never rename, delete, reinterpret or clear already recorded RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE, including old journals.

While CPU_PENDING, keep the sole permit, block all new native action batches and acceptance observations, and continue guard measurement. No new launch is possible through the held permit. Boundary awaits a guard-owned terminal decision; it must not calculate CPU thresholds or independently waive the candidate. Missing/malformed/stale evidence, owner mismatch, stop, hold, unknown state or journal failure stays fail closed.

Two consecutive CPU-unsafe samples under existing unsafeSamplesToStop confirm unsafe: emit irreversible RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE, persist existing hold and stop markers, set resourceInvalid=true, and use existing owned cleanup. Any non-CPU failure is never a recoverable CPU candidate: retain its immediate unsafe event/native refusal, set invalid-resource, and preserve existing watchdog stop cadence or fail sooner; do not relax memory, pressure, disk, swap or missing-measurement behavior.

Recommend resolving an isolated CPU candidate only after existing healthySamplesToResume (three) consecutive fully healthy watches. A new bad reading resets recovery; two consecutive bad confirms unsafe. Persist a distinct guard-owned CPU_RECOVERED event; boundary requires that explicit resolution plus the latest fresh healthy sample and unchanged identity/hold/stop checks. No action executes merely because one later event is healthy. This is a future policy clarification, not current behavior or proof the old run was safe.

Bound the whole CPU-pending episode with a monotonic deadline derived from existing knobs, e.g. (unsafeSamplesToStop + healthySamplesToResume) * watchIntervalSeconds. Current values give75seconds, enough for three normal ~16second recovery watches. Do not reset deadline on repeated spikes, stale refreshes or clock rollback. Expiry/missing confirmation invalidates and stops; use existing bounded measurement commands and owned-group grace/kill paths. Do not invent an unbounded wait or relaunch retry.

Child exit/operator stop while pending or confirmed unsafe must set resourceInvalid=true and final invalid even if child exits zero. A recovered candidate may finalize valid only with clean child outcome, proven owned cleanup, and successful journal close. A write/close or safety-marker failure retains fail-closed evidence/permit behavior. Keep every candidate/recovery/unsafe event in finalized journals; no acceptance promotion from pending files or log extracts.

Preserve the exact atomic permit, legacy-state refusal, ownership-token census, group cleanup, all preflight thresholds and sampling, and prior unsafe recovery/re-admission. No browser/GPU flags or runner migration. Document the clarified future CPU state contract and require independent review before a native run.
